title: At home
summary: Every noun is a de-word or a het-word; een goes with both. Every plural takes de. No article with an indefinite plural, with uncountables in general or with a job after zijn. Learn each noun with its article.
explain:
Dutch has two words for *the*: `de` and `het`. Which one a noun takes depends on its gender: most nouns are de-words, the rest are het-words. The word for *a* is `een` for both. Ukrainian has no articles at all, so this is a habit to build from the start.

### The forms

| | de-word | het-word |
| the (one) | de kamer | het raam |
| a (one) | een kamer | een raam |
| the (more) | de kamers | de ramen |
| (more, not known) | kamers | ramen |

- In the **plural** every noun takes `de`: `het raam`, but `de ramen`.
- `Een` has no plural: `een kamer`, but `kamers`.

> De kamer is groot. — The room is big.
> Het raam is open. — The window is open.
> De ramen zijn schoon. — The windows are clean.

### When to use de/het, een or nothing

- `de` or `het`: something known, already mentioned, or the only one there is: `het dak van ons huis`.
- `een`: one thing that is new to the listener: `We hebben een zolder.`
- **nothing**: a plural that is not known (`Ik koop stoelen`), something you cannot count, said in general (`Hout is duur`), and a job after `zijn` or `worden` (`Zij is kapper`). With an adjective a job does get een: `een goede kapper`.

> We kopen nieuwe stoelen. — We are buying new chairs.
> Mijn buurman is schilder. — My neighbour is a painter.

### Rules that help: het

- All **diminutives** (*verkleinwoorden*), even of de-words: `de kamer`, but `het kamertje`.
- An **infinitive** used as a noun: `het eten`, `het koken`.
- **Languages**: `het Nederlands`, `het Oekraïens`.
- **Metals**: `het goud`, `het ijzer`.
- Words in **-isme, -ment, -sel, -um**: `het toerisme`, `het appartement`, `het raadsel`, `het museum`. Exception: `de datum`. This is about the suffix -sel (`raadsel` from raden): in `de mossel` and `de oksel` the letters are not a suffix.
- Most two-syllable words starting with the unstressed prefix **ge-, be-, ver-**: `het gebouw`, `het begin`, `het verhaal`, `het behang`. Exception: `de verkoop`. Where the first syllable is stressed it is no prefix, and the rule does not apply: `de beker`, `de gevel`.

> Het kamertje is klein. — The little room is small.
> Na het eten zitten we op de bank. — After dinner we sit on the sofa.

### Rules that help: de

- **People and jobs**: `de man`, `de buurvrouw`, `de kapper`. But `het kind`, and `het meisje` (a diminutive).
- Words in **-ing, -heid, -ie, -tie, -teit**: `de woning`, `de gezondheid`, `de familie`, `de informatie`, `de universiteit`. But `het ding` (no ending there) and `het ministerie`.
- Words in **-erij** and most in **-ij**: `de bakkerij`, `de partij`. Exception: `het schilderij`.
- Persons in **-er, -aar, -eur**: `de bakker`, `de leraar`, `de chauffeur`. (Things in -er can be het: `het nummer`.)
- **Fruit, trees and flowers**: `de appel`, `de eik`, `de tulp`; **rivers and mountains**; **letters and numbers**: `de a`, `de drie`.

About two thirds of all nouns are de-words. For the rest there is no rule: `het plafond`, `het raam`, `het huis`. That is why the best advice is: **always learn a noun with its article**. In a compound the **last part** decides: `het bad` + `de kamer` = `de badkamer`; `de keuken` + `het raam` = `het keukenraam`.

### Why it matters

De or het decides other words too: the ending of an adjective (`een grote kamer`, but `een groot raam`), `deze/dit`, `die/dat`, `onze/ons` and `welke/welk`. You will meet each of these in its own unit.

### Watch out

- The plural is always de: *het ramen → `de ramen`.
- No een before a plural: *een stoelen → `stoelen`.
- A diminutive is always het: *de kamertje → `het kamertje`.
- A job after zijn has no article: `Hij is kapper`. (`Hij is de kapper` means he is the hairdresser you both know.)

### Compared with Ukrainian

The Ukrainian gender does not help: `місто` is neuter, but `de stad` is a de-word. Think of `de/het` as *this one we know*, `een` as *one, new*, and nothing as *things in general*.

sentences.nl: De woonkamer is licht en het raam is groot.
sentences.en: The living room is bright and the window is big.
sentences.note: Woonkamer ends in kamer, a de-word, and the last part of a compound decides: de woonkamer. Raam is a het-word you simply have to learn.

sentences.nl: Het schilderij hangt boven de bank.
sentences.en: The painting hangs above the sofa.
sentences.note: Most words in -ij are de-words, but schilderij is the well-known exception: het schilderij.

sentences.nl: We kopen gordijnen voor de slaapkamer.
sentences.en: We are buying curtains for the bedroom.
sentences.note: Gordijnen is a plural that is not known yet, so it has no article. One curtain would be een gordijn, and the curtain het gordijn.
alt: Wij kopen gordijnen voor de slaapkamer.

sentences.nl: De trap naar de zolder is erg steil.
sentences.en: The stairs to the attic are very steep.
sentences.note: English says stairs, but Dutch de trap is one word in the singular, so the verb is is. Trap and zolder are both de-words.
alt: De trap naar de zolder is heel steil.

sentences.nl: Het plafond in de badkamer is wit.
sentences.en: The ceiling in the bathroom is white.
sentences.note: Plafond is a het-word without a rule to help. Badkamer is de, because kamer is the last part.
Nouns made with the ending -ing are de-words: de verwarming, de woning, de vergadering.

sentences.nl: Mijn broer is schilder en verft vooral muren.
sentences.en: My brother is a painter and mainly paints walls.
sentences.note: A job after zijn takes no article: is schilder. Muren is a plural said in general, so no article either.

sentences.nl: Het schoonmaken van de ramen duurt lang.
sentences.en: Cleaning the windows takes a long time.
sentences.note: An infinitive used as a noun is always a het-word: het schoonmaken. De ramen is plural, so de, although it is het raam.

sentences.nl: Het kamertje boven de trap is van mijn zoon.
sentences.en: The little room above the stairs is my son's.
sentences.note: A diminutive is always a het-word, even when the noun itself is de: de kamer, het kamertje.

sentences.nl: Behang is duur, maar het is mooi.
sentences.en: Wallpaper is expensive, but it is beautiful.
sentences.note: Wallpaper in general, a thing you cannot count: no article. Behang is a het-word: be- + one syllable, like het begin.

exercises.en: The cushions are on the sofa.
exercises.note: Every plural takes de, also when the singular is a het-word: het kussen, de kussens. Een never goes with a plural.

exercises.nl: Ik zoek een lamp voor ___ woonkamer.
exercises.en: I am looking for a lamp for the living room.
exercises.note: In a compound the last part decides: de kamer, so de woonkamer. A countable noun in the singular cannot stand without an article.

exercises.nl: ___ kamertje boven de trap is klein.
exercises.en: The little room above the stairs is small.
exercises.note: A diminutive is always het, even though it is de kamer. A singular noun like this needs an article.

exercises.nl: ___ plafond in de slaapkamer is te laag.
exercises.en: The ceiling in the bedroom is too low.
exercises.note: Plafond is a het-word without a rule to show it: het plafond. Learn it together with its article.

exercises.nl: ___ (de/het) plafond in de keuken is laag.
exercises.en: The ceiling in the kitchen is low.
exercises.note: Plafond is a het-word. No rule tells you that, so learn it as one unit: het plafond.

exercises.en: The cushion is lying on the floor.
exercises.note: Vloer is a de-word, like about two thirds of all nouns: de vloer.

exercises.en: How do you say 'sofa' in Dutch?
exercises.note: The name of a language is a het-word: het Nederlands, het Oekraïens, het Engels.

exercises.nl: Na ___ (de/het) eten zitten we in de woonkamer.
exercises.en: After dinner we sit in the living room.
exercises.note: Eten here is an infinitive used as a noun, and those are always het-words: het eten.

exercises.en: The living room is very bright.
exercises.note: The last part of the compound decides: kamer is de, so de woonkamer.
In the plural het becomes de, and the verb becomes plural too: de kussens zijn.

exercises.from: Het schilderij hangt in de gang.
answers: De schilderijen hangen in de gang.
exercises.en: The paintings hang in the hall.
exercises.note: Het schilderij, but de schilderijen: every plural takes de. Hangt becomes hangen.

exercises.task: Talk about one curtain instead of several.
exercises.note: A plural that is not known has no article. One thing that is new to the listener gets een, for de-words and het-words alike.
Het raam is a het-word, but every plural takes de: de ramen.

exercises.wrong: De behang in de gang is oud.
answers: Het behang in de gang is oud.
exercises.en: The wallpaper in the hall is old.
exercises.note: Behang has two syllables and starts with be-, like het begin and het bezoek: it is a het-word.
Een means 'one' and never goes with a plural. A plural that is not known has no article at all.

exercises.wrong: Het muur in de slaapkamer is blauw.
answers: De muur in de slaapkamer is blauw.
exercises.en: The wall in the bedroom is blue.
exercises.note: Muur is a de-word: de muur. Most nouns are de-words; when you are not sure, de is the better guess.
